title: Asymptotic Homogenization of Auxetic-Core Sandwich Shells for the Isogeometric Analysis of a Rear Fuselage Structure with Embedded Engines
content: Embedding the engines in the rear fuselage is a promising concept to reduce aircraft fuel consumption, but it leads to complex load paths and can introduce engine vibrations into the fuselage skin. Sandwich panels with an auxetic metamaterial core are a potential skin concept for this region, as they can be tailored locally and enhance energy dissipation and passive vibration damping. However, modeling the individual cells for a fuselage structure leads to infeasibly large system sizes. This work therefore presents a scale-bridging analysis framework that homogenizes sandwich materials with auxetic cores into shell stiffnesses for macroscale structural design. For this, a first-order computational homoge-nization of the core combined with classical laminate theory and an asymptotic homogenization of the complete sandwich section are considered. Both are compared against a reference model with a resolved core under tension, shear and bending as well as in a modal analysis, with deviations below 6% for the asymptotic homogenization. The homogenized stiffnesses are then used in an isogeometric analysis of a rear fuselage with embedded engines. Under a 2.5 g pull-up maneuver, the core topology and its orientation directly influence the global deformation, making the core topology a design variable at the aircraft scale.
